installation.note: sh is a POSIX-compliant shell; on Debian/Ubuntu it is usually dash, on some systems a link to bash

overview.summary: sh is the standard Unix shell command interpreter. It runs scripts and commands in a POSIX-compliant way. On many Linux systems sh is dash (lightweight) or a symlink to bash; scripts that start with #!/bin/sh should be portable.
when_to_use: Start a minimal shell (dash is faster for scripts)

syntax.description: Without SCRIPT, sh starts an interactive shell (if supported). With SCRIPT, it runs the script.

options.description: Run COMMAND as a single string
Exit immediately if a command exits non-zero

examples.title: Run a portable script
examples.description: Execute script.sh with the default sh (dash or bash)

related_commands.description: Extended shell; sh is often dash or bash in sh mode
